title: The Crow and the Pitcher
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A thirsty Crow found a Pitcher with some water in it, but so little was there that, try as she might, she could not reach it with her beak, and it seemed as though she would die of thirst within sight of the remedy. At last she hit upon a clever plan. She began dropping pebbles into the Pitcher, and with each pebble the water rose a little higher until at last it reached the brim, and the knowing bird was enabled to quench her thirst.
Necessity is the mother of invention.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the thirsty Crow find?
options: A stream running through a field
A bowl of pebbles beside a road
A Pitcher with some water in it
A well with a broken rope

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why can't the Crow drink the water at first?
options: There is too little water for her beak to reach
The Pitcher is sealed with a lid
The water is too hot to drink
Another bird is guarding the Pitcher

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crow begin dropping into the Pitcher?
options: Twigs
Leaves
Seeds
Pebbles

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the water level with each pebble dropped in?
options: It stays exactly the same
It rises a little higher
It splashes out of the Pitcher
It turns cloudy and undrinkable

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Crow finally able to do once the water reaches the brim?
options: Fly away with the Pitcher
Wash the pebbles clean
Quench her thirst
Share the water with other birds

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Crow choose to drop pebbles into the Pitcher rather than give up?
options: She works out that raising the water level will let her reach it
She hopes the pebbles will break the Pitcher open
She is trying to hide the water from other birds
She wants to test how deep the Pitcher is

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Crow's success suggest about facing a difficult problem?
options: Only the strongest creatures can solve difficult problems
Waiting patiently is always the safest solution
Asking for help is faster than working alone
Careful thinking can find a way around an obstacle that brute force cannot

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the water rose to the "brim"?
options: The bottom of the Pitcher
The very top edge of the Pitcher
A crack along the side of the Pitcher
The narrow part of the Pitcher's neck

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the bird was "enabled" to quench her thirst?
options: She was forbidden from doing it
She was forced to do it quickly
She was made able to do it
She was reminded to do it later

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A real need can push someone to invent a clever solution
Birds are cleverer than most other animals
Pebbles are more useful than most people realize
Patience alone is enough to solve any problem

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crow risk if she cannot reach the water?
options: Losing the Pitcher to another bird
Being unable to fly any farther
Breaking her beak against the Pitcher
Dying of thirst within sight of the remedy

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of the Crow's body cannot reach the water at first?
options: Her wing
Her beak
Her foot
Her tail

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Crow described as once she solves the problem?
options: The frightened bird
The wandering bird
The knowing bird
The sleeping bird

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does dropping in pebbles work as a solution at all?
options: Each pebble takes up space and pushes the water level upward
The pebbles dissolve and thicken the water
The pebbles frighten the water to the surface
The pebbles crack the Pitcher so water leaks out

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Crow's persistence with the pebbles show about her character?
options: She is easily distracted from her goal
She prefers to rely on luck rather than effort
She is unwilling to try anything unfamiliar
She keeps working at the problem instead of giving up

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "quench" mean in "quench her thirst"?
options: To increase or make stronger
To satisfy or put an end to
To hide or cover up
To measure or count exactly

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Crow spills a Pitcher of water by accident
A Crow gives up trying to reach water in a Pitcher
A thirsty Crow raises the water level with pebbles until she can drink
A Crow shares her water with a passing traveller
